# Project knowledge (full)

_Pinned rows as of 2026-11-27 10:42 UTC; a row's current text: `lore show --id <id>`._

## Must rules

<rule id="rul_01a0ec2a99697af4a7163662c6972a9d" severity="must" trust="0.50">
The core module github.com/ubgo/auth requires only the Go standard library and github.com/ubgo/sqlb; any package needing another module is its own module (deps_test.go enforces it).
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a0f5ce136e79d7b7fffb7ac870f1d1" severity="must" trust="0.50">
A request for docs or a guide covers the whole library by default: getting started, concepts, every plugin, every integration, reference, operations and extending, with tested snippets. The owner's examples illustrate the kind of content wanted; they do not limit it.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cc2ff16710d866773f3d7b6541d" severity="must" trust="0.50">
No foreign keys and no ON DELETE CASCADE anywhere, on any engine, in the core or any plugin (ADR-0002, owner 2026-10-03). Tables are plain storage; a plugin with rows belonging to a user declares them through auth.UserTableOwner, and Auth.DeleteUser removes them in Go in one transaction. TestGuard_NoForeignKeys and TestGuard_UserTablesAreDeleted enforce it.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cc2ff8b78aaba2fa6d4cad495db" severity="must" trust="0.50">
Never build SQL by concatenating a table-name constant ("CREATE TABLE " + TableNameX, "REFERENCES " + ...). Every table name goes through the Auth (a.TableName(t), the renaming dialect), because auth.RenameTable and auth.WithTablePrefix rename tables per instance. TestGuard_TableNamesNeverConcatenated enforces it, and task check reruns the integration suite with every table prefixed.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cc2fffd74ab82d812130584f92c" severity="must" trust="0.50">
ubgo/auth is the universal auth library for Go, for every kind of Go app (owner 2026-10-05). Never scope or reject a feature as 'only for Go SaaS apps'; offer a different mode as an opt-in package or module with its drawbacks documented (as authgate is), never by weakening the defaults.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cc30075767c85d199d3b54de86e" severity="must" trust="0.50">
Third-party packages sit behind our interfaces and never leak into our API: an adapter (contrib/goth for oauth.Provider, contrib/redis for session stores) returns our types only, lives in its own module, and passes our conformance kit (oauthtest, sessiontest), so it can be swapped for another package without touching the core or the app.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cc300e87670b029b5e3ba4a0e10" severity="must" trust="0.50">
Choose the most flexible, extensible option (pluggable stores, typed hooks, per-instance options) unless it weakens a security guarantee (owner 2026-10-03). Every session store must keep everything the core stores on a session (sessiontest is the contract), so SQL, Redis, memory and custom stores stay interchangeable.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cc301587cae9382f1fc6c248e58" severity="must" trust="0.50">
A won't-do reason must be checked against the code before it is written or recommended (owner 2026-10-03). The won't-do review marks every row the owner decided with '👤 Owner decided (date):' at the start of its reason; nothing else gets that marker.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a10cd9cd6a716fa45db269a6f5a35d" severity="must" trust="0.50">
Feature completeness wherever possible (owner 2026-10-05): when a common auth feature or shape exists (an option, a parameter, a route), offer it too, alongside our own shape if ours differs, instead of answering 'covered differently'. Only something that weakens security is refused, or offered strictly as an explicit opt-in with its risk documented.
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a21c09b6627040bea444262a53a297" severity="must" trust="0.25" review="agent-written, not approved">
Every limit and behaviour is an option with a documented default (today's value). For a limit, 0 or empty means off or no limit, except where 0 would remove a security protection: that fails at startup naming the option. An option that existed before keeps its zero meaning, and a new no-limit gets its own name (NoLimit, NO_LIMIT). Deliberately fixed behaviours are listed with the reason (docs/reference/options.md and the module's guide). Changes stay backward compatible and ship as patch releases (owner 2026-11-27).
</rule>

<rule id="rul_01a21c99aa987d4aaa2227a9f45cf013" severity="must" trust="0.25" review="agent-written, not approved">
Full and release gates run on GitHub Actions (test.yml via workflow_dispatch) on the exact commit; locally only per-package tests. Changes land through a PR, squash-merged, one commit per change on main; release tags go on the squashed commit after a green test.yml on it. test.yml stays manual: no push or pull_request trigger without the owner's yes (owner 2026-11-27).
</rule>
